intro.title: UNINVITED COMPANY
intro.body: A rust-pocked ship closes on your port side. Weapons powered. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Hail, little ship. Cut your engines. We'll make this quick.

ai.aria: The weapons are charged in a very spirited way!
ai.marv: Their fuel reserves suggest they cannot chase us far. But far enough.
ai.rex: Threat assessment: moderate. Recommending weapons free.
ai.chip: Protection insurance add-on is available. Ask me how.
ai.ajoy: You could fight. You could flee. You could talk. One works better than you think.

choices.sub: Hargrove did the groundwork · no cost

choices.text: Flee — burn fuel, leave them behind

negotiate.title: NEGOTIATION
negotiate.body: They're listening — for now. The captain's hand hovers over the weapons panel.

ai.marv: They will not accept the first offer. Or the second.
ai.rex: If diplomacy fails I am already aiming.
ai.chip: Transcripts of this negotiation are sponsored by LipsLock™.
ai.ajoy: There is a line here you have not tried.

choices.text: Half the fuel. You let us pass

haggle.title: THE DEAL
haggle.line: Thirty percent fuel. We call it even.

ai.aria: A wonderful deal for everyone involved!
ai.marv: 30% fuel pushes our reserve below the next leg's need.
ai.rex: They are betting you will cave. Call it.
ai.chip: 30% is actually a great rate, by current space-piracy standards.
ai.ajoy: You can still walk this back. Or you can try to walk out cheaper.

pirate_prepared.title: ALREADY SETTLED
pirate_prepared.body: Hargrove reads them a registry number, a name, and a date. The channel goes quiet long enough to hear someone on the other end swallow. The weapons power down. Nobody says the word 'passage'. It happens anyway.
pirate_prepared.narrative: The pirates had already been talked to. They just hadn't known it yet. Hargrove's groundwork bought clean passage at no cost, and the crew stood a little straighter for having watched it.

pirate_paid.title: THEY PEEL OFF
pirate_paid.body: You hand over the gold. They salute — a bit too mockingly — and burn off into the dark.
pirate_paid.narrative: You hand over the gold. They salute — a bit too mockingly — and burn off into the dark.

pirate_flee.title: STRAIGHT AND FAST
pirate_flee.body: You pour the reserves into the engines. They chase for three hours, lose interest, and fall away.
pirate_flee.narrative: You pour the reserves into the engines. They chase for three hours, lose interest, and fall away.

pirate_ram.title: CONTACT
pirate_ram.body: Metal meets metal. Your hull shrieks. Theirs falls off. They drift. You drift harder — but you drift away.
pirate_ram.narrative: Metal meets metal. Your hull shrieks. Theirs falls off. They drift. You drift harder — but you drift away.

pirate_sympathy.title: A DECENT GESTURE
pirate_sympathy.body: The captain's jaw works. They lower weapons.
pirate_sympathy.line: Go. And don't come back through this sector.
pirate_sympathy.narrative: The captain's jaw works. They lower weapons and let you pass.

pirate_deal_30.title: THE DEAL IS DONE
pirate_deal_30.body: You transfer the fuel. They peel off, already haggling amongst themselves over your supplies.
pirate_deal_30.narrative: You transfer the fuel. They peel off, already haggling amongst themselves over your supplies.

pirate_deal_20.title: A BETTER DEAL
pirate_deal_20.narrative: The captain snorts and takes the smaller cut. Fine. 20.

intro.title: A COMMERCIAL OPPORTUNITY
intro.body: A merchant vessel matches your velocity with practiced ease — close enough to talk, far enough to be polite about it. Its hull is a patchwork of forty years of hard bargains. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: A trader! ARIA loves traders! They have THINGS! Things are her third favorite category!
ai.marv: MARV has assessed the vessel. Well-maintained where it counts, shabby where it doesn't. He notes this is the signature of someone good at exactly one thing.
ai.rex: REX confirms the trader's weapons are stowed. Genuinely stowed, not performatively stowed. He is cautiously unimpressed.
ai.chip: CHIP detects a fellow commercial entity! Professional courtesy protocols engaged! CHIP will be watching the margins with love!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has reviewed this trader's public ledger. Fair prices, honest scales, one incident in '61 she'll summarize on request. It involves a goat.

pitch.title: THE PITCH
pitch.body: The trader's cargo manifest scrolls across your screen — the honest parts of it, anyway. Fuel cells, sealed rations, a 'miscellaneous' category doing an enormous amount of unexamined work.

ai.aria: Look at all of it! ARIA recommends buying something! Or nothing! She just enjoys commerce as a spectacle!
ai.marv: MARV has cross-checked the prices against station rates. Fair, with a loneliness surcharge. Out here, everything has a loneliness surcharge.
ai.rex: REX notes the 'miscellaneous' category. He always notes the miscellaneous category. It is where the interesting mistakes live.
ai.chip: CHIP rates these prices 'competitive!' High praise! CHIP does not compete, CHIP wins, but still! Competitive!
ai.ajoy: AJOY recommends the fuel cells if anything. She has compared the unit price to your reserves. The comparison was not idle.

misc.title: MISCELLANEOUS
misc.body: The trader's expression shifts into something between pride and plausible deniability. A single crate is angled toward the camera. The label has been removed. Recently.
misc.line: One owner. Low mileage. No questions in either direction — that's the discount.

ai.aria: A mystery crate! ARIA is VIBRATING! Statistically it's probably fine! Statistically!
ai.marv: MARV cannot scan the crate through the trader's hull. He notes that the trader knows this. He notes the crate's placement is therefore a choice.
ai.rex: REX advises against unscannable cargo. On the record. He would also, off the record, quite like to know what it is.
ai.chip: CHIP notes 'as-is' purchases carry no warranty, no returns, and no CHIP liability! CHIP has never typed a disclaimer faster!
ai.ajoy: AJOY gives the crate forty-to-sixty odds of being worth it. She won't say which side is forty. That's the real gamble, she notes.

choices.text: Buy the crate — 15 gold, no questions
That's enough commerce for one day

trader_polite_pass.title: PLEASANTRIES EXCHANGED
trader_polite_pass.body: You swap route gossip and weather reports — there is no weather, but spacers report it anyway. The trader burns off toward softer markets.
trader_polite_pass.narrative: Route gossip exchanged. No goods changed hands, but the crew enjoyed talking to someone whose problems are different problems.

trader_ignored.title: HAIL DECLINED
trader_ignored.body: You let the hail lapse. The merchant vessel holds alongside for another minute — commercial optimism dies slowly — then peels away without ceremony.
trader_ignored.narrative: You ignored the hail. The trader moved on. Somewhere in their ledger, you are now a demographic.

trader_bought_fuel.title: TRANSACTION COMPLETE
trader_bought_fuel.body: The fuel cell crosses the gap on a cargo line, arriving with a receipt taped to it. The receipt is handwritten. The handwriting is beautiful.
trader_bought_fuel.narrative: One fuel cell, purchased fair and square. The receipt goes in the log. The cell goes in cargo. Everyone leaves solvent.

trader_bought_food.title: TRANSACTION COMPLETE
trader_bought_food.body: The ration crate arrives with a bonus tucked inside: a paper bag of actual dried fruit, unlisted on any manifest. The trader's small print, it turns out, runs in both directions.
trader_bought_food.narrative: Rations purchased, plus a gift of dried fruit that outperformed every listed item. The crew remembers this trader's name.

trader_mystery_crate.title: NO QUESTIONS ASKED
trader_mystery_crate.body: The crate arrives. It is heavier than it looks, which is the first data point you were not entitled to. It goes in the hold, label-side down, which is a joke, because there is no label.
trader_mystery_crate.line: Pleasure doing business. Whatever it turns out to be — I never said it was anything.
trader_mystery_crate.narrative: The crate is aboard. Nobody has opened it yet. 'Yet' is the operative word, and everyone aboard can hear it.

trader_declined.title: NO SALE
trader_declined.body: The trader takes the refusal with professional grace and one final, reflexive price adjustment, which you also decline.
trader_declined.narrative: No sale. The trader moved on to softer wallets. The manifest, and its miscellaneous category, remain a road not taken.

trader_bought_beacon.title: INSURANCE, PORTABLE
trader_bought_beacon.body: The beacon crosses the gap in its original case, seals unbroken. 'Previous owner never needed it,' the trader says, then, after a pause neither of you enjoys: 'Never got to it, anyway. Sixty. It's good hardware.'
trader_bought_beacon.narrative: One emergency beacon, discounted history included. It goes in the rack by the airlock — the shelf where things wait to be needed never.

intro.title: THE HERMIT OF THE LANE
intro.body: The contact isn't on any chart: a habitat cobbled from three ship hulls and what appears to be a grain silo, holding a slow tumble in the middle of nowhere. Someone lives here. Someone has lived here a long time. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: A hermit! ARIA has read about hermits! They know things! Or they've forgotten things! Either way: things!
ai.marv: MARV estimates the habitat is thirty years old and should not have survived ten. He is recalibrating something. Possibly respect.
ai.rex: REX scanned the habitat for weapons. He found a harpoon. A harpoon. He has decided not to be worried about the harpoon, and is failing.
ai.chip: CHIP has no commercial data on this individual! No purchase history! No profile! CHIP is fascinated the way scientists are fascinated by the deep sea!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes that people who live alone this far out either want company badly or want it not at all, and both kinds wave you in.

visit.title: TEA, LOOSELY DEFINED
visit.body: Inside, the habitat is dense with salvage arranged by a private taxonomy — engine parts shelved with dried flowers, star charts annotated in three colors of ink. Your host produces cups of something hot that is legally distinct from tea.

ai.aria: ARIA is recording everything! For history! And because the shelving system might be genius! Might!
ai.marv: MARV has been listening to the hermit's story for eleven minutes. He has identified four impossibilities and zero lies. He is still working on how.
ai.rex: REX accepted the hot beverage out of politeness. He has now drunk all of it, also out of politeness. He would like the record to show it was excellent.
ai.chip: CHIP asked the hermit about brand preferences! The hermit laughed for a full minute! CHIP is choosing to log it as engagement!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes your host has mentioned 'the old route' three times. She recommends asking about the old route. Gently. Wind them up and step back.

choices.text: Trade news of the inner systems
Thank them and take your leave

route.title: THE OLD ROUTE
route.body: The hermit unrolls a chart older than your ship — hand-corrected, coffee-ringed, annotated with the blunt honesty of someone who was there. A finger taps a stretch of your own route ahead.

ai.aria: Local knowledge! The BEST knowledge! ARIA is updating the nav charts and saying thank you seventeen ways!
ai.marv: MARV has checked the hermit's corrections against current survey data. The corrections are right. The survey is wrong. MARV is filing a report nobody will read.
ai.rex: REX respects intelligence gathered on foot. Or on tumble. He is committing the chart to memory as a backup to the backup.
ai.chip: CHIP notes this navigational data is being provided FREE! CHIP has checked three times! There is no catch! CHIP is dizzy!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has integrated the route notes. She estimates they'll save fuel, time, or trouble — she won't know which until it doesn't happen.

choices.text: Accept the route notes with thanks

drifter_waved.title: SHIPS THAT PASS
drifter_waved.body: You flash your running lights in the old courtesy pattern. The habitat's lights flash back — a beat late, a little crooked, unmistakably glad.
drifter_waved.narrative: You waved. They waved back. Out here, that counts as a full social season for both parties.

drifter_news.title: NEWS FROM INSIDE
drifter_news.body: You spend an hour retelling the inner systems' news — the politics, the prices, the scandal with the terraforming contract. The hermit listens like it's theater, which, told properly, it is.
drifter_news.narrative: An hour of news traded for an afternoon of perspective. The crew leaves lighter. The hermit's laughter follows you to the airlock.

drifter_left.title: A DECENT VISIT
drifter_left.body: You leave before the third cup of legally-distinct tea. The hermit sees you off from the salvage-frame porch, waving with the unhurried confidence of someone who knows you'll think about this place for weeks.
drifter_left.narrative: A visit, a warm drink, a look at another way to live. The crew talks about it for three days. Nobody says the word 'lonely.' Everybody thinks it.

drifter_route_notes.title: LOCAL KNOWLEDGE
drifter_route_notes.body: The route notes are copied to your nav computer in the hermit's careful hand-drawn style, which the computer preserves out of what can only be respect.
drifter_route_notes.narrative: The old route notes shave a clean line off the leg ahead. Thirty years of tumbling in place, and the hermit still knows the road better than the road does.

drifter_paid.title: PAYMENT REFUSED, MOSTLY
drifter_paid.body: The hermit waves off the gold twice, then accepts it on the third offer 'for the silo fund,' and immediately gives you back change in the form of a jar of preserved something.
drifter_paid.line: Take the jar. The jar is non-negotiable. The jar is the whole point of the transaction.
drifter_paid.narrative: Route notes, a jar of preserved something, and the strong suspicion you got the better end of a deal the hermit designed to lose. The jar's contents remain excellent and unidentified.

intro.title: SQUATTERS' RIGHTS
intro.body: The derelict's cargo bay lights are on, which derelicts don't do. Your scan answers why: a ship grafted to the far docking ring, engines warm, registry deleted. Somebody moved into this wreck. Somebody with opinions about visitors. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: ARIA notes the derelict is INHABITED! By pirates! This is technically an urban renewal story and ARIA is trying very hard to see it that way!
ai.marv: MARV has assessed the grafted ship: faster than yours, better armed than yours, and currently — this is the useful part — pointed the wrong way.
ai.rex: REX counts one hostile vessel and an unknown boarding party inside the wreck. He has a plan for both. The plan is aggressive. Both plans are aggressive. It is one plan.
ai.chip: CHIP notes that salvage law and squatters' rights genuinely conflict here! A fascinating legal question that CHIP recommends resolving from a great distance!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has read the pirates' hail twice. They expected you to run at the word 'claimed.' She notes, for whatever it's worth, that they've already repeated themselves.

choices.text: Open fire on the grafted ship
Negotiate a split of the salvage

choices.sub: Hargrove did the groundwork · no toll

parley.title: THE SPLIT
parley.body: The pirates' negotiator meets your diplomat channel-to-channel. The opening positions are far apart: they propose keeping everything, your diplomat proposes them keeping less than everything. Civilization proceeds from there.

ai.aria: Negotiation! ARIA is rooting for everyone! Mostly you! But everyone!
ai.marv: MARV calculates the pirates' position is weaker than their tone. They've stripped the easy bays already; what's left needs cutting gear. Yours is better. Mention the cutting gear.
ai.rex: REX stands ready in case diplomacy fails. He would like the record to reflect that he thinks diplomacy is about to succeed, and that he has feelings about that.
ai.chip: CHIP is drafting the salvage-partition agreement in real time! It has clauses! Everyone loves clauses once they have them!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes their negotiator keeps glancing off-channel — checking with someone. That means there's a decision-maker, and the decision-maker is listening. Speak to the room.

choices.text: Offer the aft sections — take the bow

boarding_prepared.title: PRIOR ARRANGEMENT
boarding_prepared.body: Hargrove mentions a name. The squatters mention a different name. Hargrove mentions the first name again, more slowly. The forward bays are yours, no toll, and someone even points out the coolant corridor unprompted.
boarding_prepared.narrative: Salvaged the forward bays under a prior arrangement nobody remembers making. Hargrove's groundwork paid the toll in advance.

boarding_toll.title: PAID PASSAGE
boarding_toll.body: The gold transfers. The pirates wave you toward the unstripped forward bays with the magnanimity of landlords, and even point out which corridor floods with coolant on a timer. Almost hospitable. Almost.
boarding_toll.narrative: You paid the toll and salvaged the forward bays under pirate supervision. Strangest afternoon of the voyage, and not unprofitable.

boarding_split.title: PARTITIONED
boarding_split.body: The agreement lands: they keep the aft sections they've dug into, you take the bow. CHIP's contract is transmitted, mocked openly, and — notably — followed to the letter by both sides.
boarding_split.narrative: Salvage rights negotiated with pirates, in writing. The diplomat has asked for the contract to be framed. The request is under consideration.

boarding_left.title: THEIR WRECK NOW
boarding_left.body: You disengage and burn away. Behind you, the derelict's lights stay on — someone's home now, by the only law that operates this far out, which is presence.
boarding_left.narrative: You left the squatters their wreck. The salvage charts get one more annotation: OCCUPIED. DISPUTED. SKIP.
